### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **9** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **113** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`, `packages/platform-objects/src/pages/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/README.md`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**76** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6d7f4df3c91c0d4e7d0a40c3b5dc796290e90a2d`.

⛔ **16** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`, `packages/platform-objects/src/pages/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/README.md`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `isSystem (5 routes)`
- **4** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 38 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 40 pages)`, `/api/v1/data (route, 40 pages)`, `/api/v1/meta (route, 39 pages)`
- **25** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **152** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6d7f4df3c91c0d4e7d0a40c3b5dc796290e90a2d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1a21c38bdb33dad427f332f09713a4df018b7feb` — the merge of head `23e450a684f778f8eb84a575049aeb6cc21832e3` into base `6d7f4df3c91c0d4e7d0a40c3b5dc796290e90a2d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1a21c38bdb33dad427f332f09713a4df018b7feb && git checkout 1a21c38bdb33dad427f332f09713a4df018b7feb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6d7f4df3c91c0d4e7d0a40c3b5dc796290e90a2d 23e450a684f778f8eb84a575049aeb6cc21832e3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6d7f4df3c91c0d4e7d0a40c3b5dc796290e90a2d && git merge --no-ff 23e450a684f778f8eb84a575049aeb6cc21832e3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6d7f4df3c91c0d4e7d0a40c3b5dc796290e90a2d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6d7f4df3c91c0d4e7d0a40c3b5dc796290e90a2d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `976023f0da021d12a5e02ee7d45ff1cb15a620c1`
Local-runs: none

Reviewed read-only: the PR's body and file list, the net three-dot diff against `origin/main` (merge base `01a3421f42`; 74 files, +411 / −3330 — the body's 70 / +325 / −3275 at `016d329a36` plus patch round 1's four files, +86 / −55), card #23056 with every comment through the S8 dev report 6143150671, the named #15204 records (6118994290, 6110777865, 6116546399, 6136812787), ADR-0131, ADR-0086 and ADR-0087 on `main`, the WHICH LEVEL prose in `pr-automation.yml`, `clause2-line.mjs`, and the head's check-runs. The head had not moved past `976023f0da` at the time of writing. Patch round 1's report was still pending; its four commits (`5bd2d8d79a`, `f850dd11b5`, `a29bede970`, `976023f0da`) and its `main` merge (`891d2d55ab`, 13 `main` commits) are judged on the diff.

**Gate verdicts on this head** (polled 2026-10-13T12:27Z): 34 success, 5 skipped, 1 still running. Green: TypeScript Type Check, Lint & Repo Gates (every Lint and Type Check lane), Build Core, Build Docs, Test Core 1/6, 2/6, 4/6, 5/6, 6/6, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard (its `pull_request` leg is an early warning that exits 0 by design), the card and single-writer claim checks, Check Documentation Links. Still running: **Test Core (3/6)**. Skipped under #22998 and the pin filter: the three Dogfood Regression Gate shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Console Pin Gate — so no dogfood suite ran on this head in CI; the dev's focused dogfood run (`anonymous-door-sweep`, `permission-metadata-door-reaches-catalog`, `wall-catalog-refusal`, 41 tests) is on `016d329a36`, before the last `main` merge.

### ① Derived judgments

**The retirement — right, with two consequences the changeset should name.**
- Unregistered in the diff: `manifest.ts`'s `securityObjects` drops `SysPosition`, `SysCapability`, `SysPermissionSet`, `SysPositionPermissionSet`; the four object files, `sys-position.page.ts` and `walled-catalog-data-door.test.ts` are deleted; `objects/index.ts` and `platform-objects/pages/index.ts` drop the exports; the manifest's `pages: [SysPositionDetailPage]` goes; the three Setup nav entries become `type: 'url'` (a legal `UrlNavItemSchema` variant) opening `/apps/setup/metadata/TYPE?scope=environment`; the seven generated translation bundles and the i18n extract config follow. Tables and rows stay (no DDL in the diff) — ADR-0131 D3 and D10 as claimed.
- The changeset names every published surface that disappears, FROM → TO: the data and REST routes of all four names, the Setup nav targets and the `sys_position` record page, object permissions on the four names, and the removed exports per package (`SysPosition` and siblings, `SysPositionDetailPage`, `SystemObjectName.POSITION` / `PERMISSION_SET`, the names leaving `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE` and the derived `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_OBJECT_NAMES`, `isRowActive` / `ActivatableRow`). "An object permission on one of the four names grants nothing and can be deleted" is accurate: `defineStack`'s grant check (`collectPermissionGrantObjectErrors`) admits platform names by prefix (`isPlatformObjectName`), and no lint error reads permission-set object keys, so nothing refuses such a grant — delete is advice, not a forced migration.
- **Not named** (recommended, in the changeset): (a) `@objectstack/objectql`'s published export `PLATFORM_OBJECT_TENANCY` (objectql `index.ts:560`) loses its `sys_permission_set` row and the three other names — the body says "the tenancy entry", the changeset's removed-exports list does not; (b) on an upgraded deployment `os migrate plan`'s unmanaged-table sweep now lists the four tables (reserved prefix, declared by nothing) — report-only, never a drop (`unmanaged-tables.ts` header), which the PR's own re-pin of `unmanaged-tables.integration.test.ts` states ("the sweep is RIGHT to report it") and the changeset does not.
- **ADR-0087 disposition — right in kind and complete for its reader.** The marker is `registered catalog-row-objects-retired`, a semantic entry (`18.catalog-row-objects-retired.ts`, new in this diff; `surface` carries no backticks). Semantic is the right kind: the retired surface includes REST data routes and Setup pages, which no compiler carries, and the body prescribes a migration (a FROM → TO block), which refuses `no-migration-prescription`; `runtime-export-retired` would cover only the TS exports. The entry's `surface`, `replacement`, `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria` cover the data-door client, the object-permission author and the seed-row author; the TS export retirements are compiler-carried (ADR-0087 D9) and are listed in the changeset body, where the gate judges named operands, not every removal.

**The unwiring (E1 → A) — right; no live caller; one wording error.**
- `security-plugin.ts` at the head imports none of `permission-set-projection`, `position-write-through`, `position-environment-backfill`, `walled-catalog-data-door`; registers no middleware on `sys_permission_set` / `sys_position` / the walled set; calls neither `registerPermissionSetProjection` nor `reconcilePermissionSetProjection`; and no longer hooks `runOneTimePositionEnvironmentBackfill`. `envProjectionWired` is gone with the projector. The `writesExecutedByDataDoor` WeakSet stays, inert (7a/7b, as named).
- Guarantees: the data-door write-through ran inside the security middleware, the two-doors gate and the delegated-admin gate, and translated an authorized data write into a metadata save; after S8 the data door answers `404 OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` to every caller before any of that — strictly narrower, no authorization or tenancy path widens. The walled data-door `403` below `PLATFORM_ADMIN` on `group` / `isolated` becomes that same `404`; the `/meta` wall (`walledCatalogWriteVerdict`), the clone door and the `/packages` doors are untouched by the diff. The projector's evaluator echo (`syncEvaluatorRegistry`) is replaced by the metadata door's own registry write-through — the premise of 6110777865 — pinned on `main` by S8-T's `permission-metadata-door-reaches-catalog.dogfood.test.ts`, green on the dev's focused run at `016d329a36`; **not re-run by CI on this head** (dogfood shards skipped).
- Boot-time code that still names the retired objects, each checked at the head: `catalog-reference-report.ts` guards every scan with `engine.getObject` (`has(POSITION_OBJECT)`), so it lists `sys_position` under `absent` and skips the positions leg; `grant-permission-set-name-backfill.ts` returns `objects-absent` silently when `sys_permission_set` is unregistered, so the "one-time" backfill is now a permanent no-op that re-reads its ledger each boot and never records (C7b's rewrite replaces it, as the E6 message now says); `auto-org-admin-grant.resolvePermissionSetIdsForName` swallows the read in `tryFind` (debug) and its by-id legs go empty (C7b); `delegated-admin-gate.positionById` / `loadSetRowById` are reached only from the `sys_position_permission_set` binding gate, and the per-object gates in `security-plugin.ts` (`:6753`, `:6823`, `:7075`, `:7123`) only from writes on retired names — unreachable (8-post).
- **Wording error in the PR body and acceptance notes:** "the now-unreferenced `permission-set-projection.ts`, `position-write-through.ts`" is false for both. `catalog-reference-report.ts:83` imports `POSITION_OBJECT` and `metadataDoorAcceptsPositionName` from `position-write-through.js`; `packaged-permission-set-overlay-detection.ts:68` imports `tryFind` and `ProjectionLogger` from `permission-set-projection.js`; `position-environment-backfill.ts:70` imports from `position-write-through.js`; plugin-security's `index.ts:82,88` still exports the projector functions. No behaviour rides on this, but 7a/7b (#22975) must re-home those four symbols before deleting the modules — carry it there by name.

**E3 — right.** `sys_user_permission_set.permission_set_id` is `Field.text({ required: false, maxLength: 255, hidden: true })`; both indexes (`:284` unique, `:287`) and the description's D10 clause stay. No reader treats it as a lookup: `bootstrap-platform-admin.hasLegacySetId` reads it as an opaque id; the backfill reads it as an id key and then asks the catalog object through its guard; `position-binding-conversion.ts` reads `sys_position_permission_set.permission_set_id` as a pure-function input (D10). `Field.lookup('sys_permission_set')` survives only in the test-only legacy testkit.

**E6 — right, one edge not measured.** `bootstrapPlatformAdmin` reads no catalog row; `legacyAdminRowUnreadable` and `admin_permission_set_unreadable` are gone; leg C scans `{ permission_set: null }` and keeps a row only when `grantSetNameOf` is undefined, `hasLegacySetId` is true and the holder is an unscoped human; `findExistingPlatformAdmin` passes `reachUnnamed: false`. A fresh `single` boot promotes (S8-T's fresh-boot golden on `main`); an unnamed legacy grant of ANY set now withholds — the stricter reading, said in the code and in the changeset. Edge: D's leg C selected by id and so reached a grant whose name column is blank `''` as well as `NULL`; S8's selects `NULL` only, while the backfill's own scan treats `''` as unnamed too. A blank-named, legacy-id-bearing unscoped grant no longer withholds. On the hook's write rules a blank beside an id means the id resolved no row inside an org-less wall, so it is unlikely to be the administrator's grant — NOT MEASURED; name it to C7b with the rewrite.

**D's landed form — right.** `cleanupPackagePermissions` keeps D's `declared?: { permission }` (`UninstallDeclared`, captured by `captureUninstallDeclared` in both doors on `main`), drops the catalog-row read, the position-binding delete and the by-id grant leg, revokes by the declared names alone, and `sets` / `positionBindings` are documented as always 0; the `removed` sum in `security-plugin.ts` follows. The diff touches `packages/metadata-protocol/src/packaged-base-regime.ts` only (one refusal string) — `protocol.ts` and `index.ts` untouched, no `cloud-connection` file — as claimed.

**Spec changes — three prose, two narrowings, no dangling importer.** `permission.zod.ts` (`describe`), `permission.form.ts` (`helpText`) and `auth-config.zod.ts` (`describe`) are prose, with the three reference pages regenerated. `platform-object-names.ts` and `system-names.ts` narrow (four names, two enum members). `git grep` at the head finds no code use of `SystemObjectName.POSITION` / `PERMISSION_SET`, `SysPositionDetailPage`, `isRowActive` / `ActivatableRow` or the four object exports outside CHANGELOGs, comments and the dogfood matrix's prose fields.

**ADR-0086 anchor line — true, anchor-valid, one line, and a governed path.** The D3 row's claim stays true (`permission.zod.ts#managedBy` still holds `packageId` and `managedBy`); the dead anchor on the deleted object file is replaced by `18.catalog-row-objects-retired.ts`, which this PR adds, and the row now says the row object is retired. It is the only hunk in the file. ⚠️ `docs/adr/**` is a Tier H row of `GOVERNED_SURFACES` (`check-governed-merges.mjs:1177`; AGENTS.md Multi-agent discipline §14), so **this PR is governed by path, not only by size**. Neither the PR body ("纯代码层改动", Tier H by size) nor the card ("Neither touches a governed surface") says so, and the dev report's "no governed path among the 70 files" predates the line. The landing bar does not move (an authorized approval is what Tier H by size already needs, and the merge-queue guard refuses without it), but the ACCEPT and 维护者速读 must state the governed path and the reason the line is in a code PR (`check:adr-anchors` would otherwise red on the deleted anchor).

**Patch round 1's test re-pins — each faithful.**
- `explain-principal-person.test.ts` (added by #23202 after S8-T): the three imports move to `__tests__/legacy-catalog-objects.testkit.js`; the suite's registered-object list and assertions are unchanged. The same shape S8-T applied to its sibling Explain suites; the suite pins #23202's wording, not the catalog.
- `unmanaged-tables.integration.test.ts`: the negative control `sys_permission_set` becomes `sys_user_permission_set`, and the declared-list assertion follows. Faithful — the control must be a table the composed plugin declares — and its comment records the consequence (the retired table is now a true positive).
- `schema-migrate.host-composition.integration.test.ts`: the drift fixture moves from `sys_position`'s `(name)` unique to `sys_audience_binding_suggestion`'s organization-respelled `(package_id, permission_set_name, anchor)` unique, with both index names from `buildIndexName`; the pending-table pins move to `sys_user_position` / `sys_user_permission_set`; the absence pin (zero rows after a plan) moves to the two assignment tables plus the fixture row count; `hasTable` moves to `sys_user_permission_set`. Each pin keeps its predicate on a table the plugin still declares and on the same `replace_unique_index` plan arm.
- **A fresh boot creates no `sys_permission_set` table after S8:** at the head no object outside the test-only testkits declares it (the CLI inventory reads it by raw SQL on an existing database only), and S8-T's fresh-boot golden holds only the plugin's own objects. Nothing to re-pin was hiding a defect.

**Published text the change makes false.** The plugin-security README (in `files`) is corrected in this PR — right. Carried by name: the hand-written `content/docs` pages and ADRs (#22976, #22978), including `system-context.mdx` row 55b. **The `18.walled-catalog-tenant-writes-retired.ts` clause is not carryable: fix it in this PR.** Its `surface` ends "and a data-door insert, update or delete on sys_position, sys_permission_set and sys_capability through @objectstack/plugin-security" and its `acceptanceCriteria` says "A data-door create on sys_position or sys_permission_set by the same caller answers 403 PERMISSION_DENIED and stores nothing". Both are false the moment this lands: that door answers `404 OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`, which this diff's own entry says in the same v18 ledger. v18 is unreleased (pre mode); both entries project into one v18 upgrade guide and `spec-changes.json` at publish (ADR-0087 D4, amended 2026-10-09), so a 17 → 18 upgrader meets a 403 criterion that answers 404. The entry is `packages/spec` source, not a release-owned path (AGENTS.md's guardrails name `content/docs/releases/` and `CHANGELOG.md`; registry entries are "your PR's input"), and shipped `17.*` / `18.*` entries are edited on `main` as a matter of course (twelve modify commits in the recent log, e.g. `3f694715ee fix(spec): the … migration text names …`). The "release-text" exception the dev classified it under does not apply, and the entry's owner is not an exemption from the rule the dev itself applied to the README. It is a two-string edit in a package this PR already touches, with no committed artifact to regenerate.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` in the PR body and the changeset is the right declaration in the right spelling: `clause2-line.mjs`'s arm reads `no (narrowing)` as "not a widening, but breaking". No widening remains in the diff: every touched `index` removes (core security, plugin-security objects, platform-objects pages), the early build's one widening (`declaredCatalogItemsOf`) is D's `captureUninstallDeclared` on `main`, and the new lint test exports nothing. The `check-changeset-no-major` level axis stands down on `no`; Check Changeset is green.
- Breaking-ness is carried as the window requires: the `**BREAKING**` banner, the ADR-0087 `registered` marker, `major` refused.
- Levels against WHICH LEVEL: `plugin-security`, `platform-objects`, `spec`, `core` `minor` — each removes a published export (breaking, shipped as `minor` under the launch-window convention) — right. `metadata-protocol` `patch` (one refusal string), `service-settings` `patch` (help text), `plugin-sharing` `patch` (a private bypass set) — right. `lint` `patch` — the published rule `capability-reference-unknown` narrows its silent set (a `sys_capability` seed row no longer counts), no API change; WHICH LEVEL forces `minor` only for additive widening, the body names the behaviour, and the new seed-row test pins it — admissible. `objectql` `patch` — **arguable**: `PLATFORM_OBJECT_TENANCY` is a published export whose record loses four keys, a narrowing of a public constant; read strictly it is breaking and the window ships that as `minor`. The `fixed` group releases at the highest bump, so the published version is `minor` either way; recommended, not blocking: grade objectql `minor` and name the keys in the changeset.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev deviations, each answered:** no stacked PR (seat correction 6140398039; the PR is off `main` after S8-T landed) — right. The walled data-door refusal unregistered beyond the rulings' list, with its suite deleted here (seat-confirmed) — right: it guards only retired objects, and the `/meta` wall pin (`wall-catalog-refusal`) spans 403 → 404. The README correction beyond S8's original commit — right, the rule the dev cites applies to the walled entry too (above). `Clause-②` moved from `yes (narrowing)` to `no (narrowing)`, `metadata-protocol` to `patch`, `cloud-connection` dropped — right on D's form. Scoped re-verification after later `main` merges per AGENTS.md §10 — accepted as evidence, with the gap below. Model-free trailers — green in the Lint lanes.
- **Open question, walled module → A (seat):** consistent with E1 → A; the module, its ADR anchor and row 55b stay alive; nothing in the diff contradicts it.
- **Out-of-scope findings, carriers:** #22975 (7a/7b) — add the four helper symbols named in ①; 8-post — the per-object gates, `SYSTEM_ROW_PROVENANCE`, comment residue; C7b (#22937 / #15211) — the CLI inventory, `resolvePermissionSetIdsForName`, the grant-name backfill (now permanently `objects-absent`), the by-id uninstall leg, and the blank-name leg C edge; the docs sweep #22976 / #22978 — the hand-written pages and ADRs; the walled semantic entry — **this PR**, not a carrier.
- **Act before the queue (two):** ① correct the two data-door clauses of `18.walled-catalog-tenant-writes-retired.ts` in this PR; ② state in the ACCEPT and 维护者速读 that the diff touches `docs/adr/**` (one anchor line) and is governed Tier H by path as well as by size. A delta record on the new head.
- **Recommended, in this PR:** the changeset names `PLATFORM_OBJECT_TENANCY`'s four keys and `os migrate plan`'s report of the four tables; objectql graded `minor`; the body's "now-unreferenced" corrected for the two modules still imported. Also `scripts/check-keyed-text-bounds.mjs`: the `MEASURED` record now carries `ref: 'eab7236ff7'` (a `main` tree where the four objects still exist) beside counts taken on this branch, so the header's own recipe ("run today's instrument against that tree") and its sentence "Re-derived at MEASURED.ref on 2026-08-29: 113/118/255/594/151 — exactly the record" no longer reproduce the record this diff writes; repoint `ref` to a tree the five counts hold on, or state the two-tree recipe and correct that sentence.
- **NOT MEASURED:** objectui beyond the pin `1fb1ced362` and no browser run of the console against S8 (the nav `url` targets are read off the pin, not driven); the dogfood suites on this head (CI skips them; the dev's focused run is on `016d329a36`, before the `main` merge `891d2d55ab`); `pnpm lint` repo-wide (CI's, green); the blank-name leg C edge; Test Core (3/6) was still running at write time — the seat reads its conclusion before the queue.

Adopted by `domain:engine` seat 2 at 2026-10-13T12:30Z, after a tool-use audit of the isolated reviewer's transcript: reads, `git fetch` into a review ref, and one record write. It made no GitHub write and ran no build, test or gate. The seat takes both act-before-queue items and the recommended ones. The S8 dev patches `18.walled-catalog-tenant-writes-retired.ts`'s two data-door clauses, the changeset (objectql's `PLATFORM_OBJECT_TENANCY`, and `os migrate plan`'s unmanaged listing), and `check-keyed-text-bounds.mjs`'s record header. The seat corrects the PR body: governed by path (`docs/adr/**`) as well as by size, and "now-unreferenced". A delta record runs on the new head before the Tier H kit.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b22a9ee6bf46c680efe30b83f7937007330b5ac7`
